title: Mark a line 50 mm from a board's edge with a combination square and pencil
instruction: Draw a line 50 mm in from the board's near edge and parallel to it, at least 90 mm long, with the combination square and the pencil: seat the square's head on the edge, hold the pencil's lead on the board against the end of the blade, and slide both along together. Then stand the pencil back in its block and let go of everything.
context: Carpenters (about 0.7 million US workers, BLS 47-2031) mark a line a set distance in from an edge many times a day: to rip a board narrower, or to lay out a shelf dado or the back of a notch. On a run of identical boards the combination square is set once to 50 mm and used as the gauge: press the head's face on the edge, set the pencil on the board against the blade's end, and slide square and pencil along together. Unlike scribing to a wall, both tools move, and the offset is held only by the head's face staying tight on the board's own edge. It takes both hands: one keeps the head on the edge and pushes the square along, the other keeps the lead down and against the blade's end at the same pace. If the head lifts or turns off the edge the line steps off its distance; if the pencil leaves the blade's end it wanders. The skill is two hands each keeping its own contact over a 100 mm path in step.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. Nothing is clamped. (1) Board: a 610 mm (2 ft) offcut of a nominal 1-by-6 pine board (3/4 x 5-1/2 in actual, 19.05 x 139.7 mm; about US$10 for a 6 ft board), lying flat along y, centred at (270, 0): near edge at x 200.2, far edge at x 339.8, top 19.05 mm up, 0.73 kg (est). (2) Square: a STANLEY 46-012 12 in combination square (about US$15; listing: 12 in blade; est: blade 304.8 x 25.4 x 1.6 mm with graduations, cast head 112 x 62 x 33 mm with a knurled locking screw, 0.35 kg), its screw locked so the blade's end sticks 49 mm out from the head's 90-degree face (the 2 mm lead then lands its centre 50 mm in). The head and blade are drawn as one body. It lies on the table with the head's face at x 170.2, 30 mm off the edge, centred at y -113, the blade flat over the board 0.15 mm above its face, the 256 mm tail running back toward the arms. (3) Pencil: a flat red carpenter's pencil (the common 7 in kind such as Dixon's, about US$1; 7 x 18 mm section, worn down to 140 mm, chisel point 2 mm thick, 14 g, est), standing tip down in its block at (400, -160): a 50 x 36 x 45 mm hardwood block fixed to the table, slot 21 x 10 mm, 42 mm deep to a 3 mm floor (est). Nothing else is on the table. Checks before the first trial (ruler, calipers, kitchen scale, straightedge, incline); use the parts only if all pass: board 19 mm thick within 1 mm, 139 to 141 mm wide, 0.6 to 0.9 kg; the blade's end 49 mm from the head's face within 0.5 mm, the face flat on a straightedge with no light, the square stands on its head and blade without tipping, 0.30 to 0.39 kg; the square on the board slides down an incline of the board tilted to 15 to 22 degrees (friction 0.27 to 0.40); the pencil's lead makes a mark on the board and the pencil stands in its block without help and lifts out with a straight pull.
scoring: A pencil line cannot be drawn in the simulator. The sim therefore reads the poses of the board, square, pencil and block, the grippers and the pencil-on-board contact force, and scores the PATH of the pencil's lead tip (its offset from the board's edge, straightness, length) while the square's head is held against the edge; the real trial reads the pencil's own line with a ruler and a straightedge, and an end photo. Ink (sim, a declared rule): each step the lead's tip is on the board's top face (within 0.3 mm, or pressed into it), over that face, with the pencil within 20 degrees of upright, AND the contact force between pencil and board is 0.3 N or more (a force that cannot be read counts as none), that point is on the line; a hovering tip marks nothing. Seated: the head's face within 1.0 mm of the edge, turned within 1.5 degrees of it, lying flat within 3 degrees (real: no light under the face). Guided: a line point is guided if on that step the square is seated and the pencil's flat face lies on the blade's end (gap -1.2 to +0.8 mm) within 9 mm of the blade's middle (real: the pencil is seen against the blade's end). Guided OK: of the 2 mm stretches along the line, 95 percent or more hold ink and every ink point in them was guided, so a line drawn without the square on the edge scores nothing. Spans: the line is at least 90 mm long with no gap over 6 mm (real: ruler). Parallel: the straight line fitted through the points within 1 degree of parallel to the edge (real: its distance from the edge at its two ends differs by under 2 mm). Straight: every point within 1.5 mm of that line (real: straightedge). At 50 mm: the fitted line 50 mm in from the edge within 2 mm at both ends (real: ruler). Stowed: the pencil back in its block, tip within 3 mm of the slot's axis and 5 mm of its floor, axis within 10 degrees of upright. Hands off: both grippers' finger zones 30 mm or more from the square, pencil and block on every step of the last 1 s. Still: square and pencil each move under 5 mm over the last 1 s. Latches, at any step: the board moved 20 mm or turned 3 degrees, or any part more than 3 mm below the table top. Score: 0 if a latch fired or the square was never seated for 0.5 s; 0.25 if it was seated but there is no good line; 0.5 if the line is good (spans, guided, parallel, straight, 50 mm in) but the pencil is not stowed at the last step; 0.75 if good and stowed but hands off or still fails on a step of the last 1 s (20 steps); 1.0 if good, stowed, hands off and still on every step of the last 1 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with contact friction. Board: one loose 0.73 kg box. Square: one loose 0.35 kg body (head, locking-screw knob, blade with marks; the screw is locked, so no sliding). Pencil: one loose body, chisel point as steps. A pencil line cannot be drawn in the simulator: the one declared rule is ink, the lead tip on the board under a PhysX contact force of 0.3 N or more.
reset_notes: Wipe or sand off the pencil line, or turn the board over to a clean face. Set the square down with its head's face 30 mm off the near edge, centred at y -113, the blade over the board, still locked at 49 mm. Stand the pencil in its block at (400, -160). The checks in setup are done once per new board, square or pencil.
